config.title: Event Handling

intro.title: Event Handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component with interactive buttons that respond to user clicks. You will learn how to handle events in Angular using event binding syntax, such as (click), to trigger functions in your TypeScript code. The core concept involves capturing user interactions and updating the component's state or UI in response. By the end, you'll have a working app that demonstrates basic event handling with clear visual feedback.
intro.usecase: Event handling is fundamental to creating interactive Angular applications that respond to user actions. In real-world software, you'll implement event handlers for form submissions in login screens, button clicks in e-commerce checkout flows, and filter changes in data dashboards. Developers use event binding to capture user interactions like menu selections, modal closures, and real-time search inputs. Mastering event handling allows you to build responsive interfaces where user actions trigger immediate UI updates and business logic execution.

objectives: Implement event binding syntax to connect DOM events to component methods
Construct event handler methods in TypeScript to process user interactions
Apply the $event object to access and utilize event data within handlers
Configure event handling for common UI events like click, input, and keyup
Integrate event handling with component state to update the view dynamically
Manipulate the DOM by controlling element visibility or styles through event-driven logic
Initialize and bind custom events between parent and child components

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core and @angular/common
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct module paths. You'll need both imports for creating an Angular component and using common directives.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component from @angular/core and CommonModule from @angular/common
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular dependencies are imported for component creation and template directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some dependencies, but make sure you have both: Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main component class with selector and template
steps.instruction: Create a component class named EventHandlingComponent with the selector 'app-event-handling' and an empty inline template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the selector and template. The template can be an empty string for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class with the correct selector and an empty template is created.
successCriteria: The component class EventHandlingComponent is defined with selector 'app-event-handling' and an empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component class is named EventHandlingComponent and has the selector 'app-event-handling' with an empty template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you've used @Component with the correct selector and template.

steps.title: Initialize component state with a message property
steps.instruction: Inside the EventHandlingComponent class, add a public property named 'message' of type string and set its initial value to 'Click the button!'.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body, like: message: string = 'Click the button!';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state property that can be displayed and updated later.
successCriteria: The EventHandlingComponent class contains a public 'message' property with type string and initial value 'Click the button!'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've declared a property named 'message' with the correct type (string) and initial value ('Click the button!').
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't have the required property. Add a public property named 'message' of type string with initial value 'Click the button!' inside the EventHandlingComponent class.

steps.title: Add a button element to the template
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Click Me' to the component template.
steps.hint: In Angular, you add HTML elements directly inside the template string. Use the <button> tag.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button to a template
<button>Submit</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a button element with the text 'Click Me'.
successCriteria: A <button>Click Me</button> element is present in the component's template property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Click Me' inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element with text 'Click Me' is missing from the template. Add it inside the template string.

steps.title: Wire the button click event to the handler method
steps.instruction: Add (click) event binding to the button element in your template to call the handleClick method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (event)="handler()". For click events, use (click)="handleClick()".
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: binding a click event to a method
<button (click)="onButtonClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button in the template will have a click event bound to the handleClick method.
successCriteria: The button element includes (click)="handleClick()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct event binding syntax: (click)="handleClick()".
steps.feedbackWrong: The button click event isn't properly bound to the handler method. Check that you're using (click)="handleClick()" syntax.

steps.title: Display the message property in the template
steps.instruction: Add interpolation {{ message }} to the component's template to display the current message value.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces with the property name inside the template to display its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will display the current message value using Angular interpolation.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation {{ message }} that displays the component's message property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the interpolation syntax {{ message }} in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required interpolation. Add {{ message }} to display the message property.

steps.title: Add an input element for text entry
steps.instruction: Add an input element with type='text' to the template, after the button.
steps.hint: Use the HTML <input> tag with the type attribute set to 'text'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a text input in a template
<input type="text">
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a text input element for user input.
successCriteria: An <input type="text"> element is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure it has type='text'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or incorrect. Add <input type="text"> to the template.

steps.title: Create an input change handler method
steps.instruction: In the EventHandlingComponent class, define a method named handleInput that takes an event parameter and updates the message property with the input's value.
steps.hint: The method should accept an event parameter of type Event and use event.target.value to get the input text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleInput method that updates the message based on user input.
successCriteria: The EventHandlingComponent class contains a handleInput method that updates the message property with the input value from an event.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleInput method accepts an event parameter and updates the message property with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInput method is missing or incorrect. Check that you've defined a method named handleInput in the component class that updates the message property.

steps.title: Wire the input event to the change handler
steps.instruction: Add an (input) event binding to the input element that calls handleInput() with $event.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (input)="handleInput($event)". This will call your handler whenever the user types in the input field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: binding an input event to a handler
<input (input)="onInputChange($event)">
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will now trigger the handleInput method whenever the user types, capturing real-time input.
successCriteria: The input element has an (input) event binding that calls handleInput($event).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added (input)="handleInput($event)" to the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element needs an event binding. Use Angular's (input) syntax to call handleInput with $event.
